changes.current_line: Every payout reconciles automatically to its transactions and your ERP.
changes.change: For finance buyers (CFO/controller), make this the lead message: "Stop spending month-end on a week of archaeology. Every deposit matches automatically to its transactions and the invoices in your ERP, so you close the month faster."
changes.why: Payout-to-ERP reconciliation was the only part of the pitch that got a reaction, and the CFO herself described the pain as a nine-day close and 'a week of archaeology' spent matching deposits by hand.

changes.current_line: Financial infrastructure to grow globally, in every currency.
changes.change: For finance-led, domestic mid-market buyers, open with the CFO's words instead: "Know where your money is." Keep M1 for global or multi-currency accounts only.
changes.why: The 'financial infrastructure, global growth, all the currencies' opener drew silence from a three-state distributor, while the CFO stated her need as 'I just want to know where my money is.'

changes.current_line: Proven ROI, backed by an independent economic impact study.
changes.change: For finance buyers, lead with an offer instead of a generic study: "We'll build the cost of your month-end from your own statements and staff costs: your number, not ours." Do not quote a figure until a validated one is on file.
changes.why: The deal turned when the CFO asked to see it with her own data and called the resulting business case 'my number, not yours', which means the method persuaded her and generic proof did not.

changes.current_line: Trusted by leading businesses; see our customer stories.
changes.change: For wholesale and distribution buyers, stop leading with retail customer stories. Until we have a distributor reference, point to the own-data business case (see M6) instead of unrelated logos.
changes.why: The CFO asked to speak to another distributor, and the retail case study backfired ('this is a company that sells sweaters'). We never got her a reference call.
